question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Using hieroglyphs to write, the ancient Egyptians noted down measurements with units like the remen, a unit of ______ and the heqat, a unit of volume. The remen, for example, appears as a hieroglyph resembling a bird's leg that ends in a long, clawed foot.
option a: area, the djeba; a unit of length,
option b: area the djeba, a unit of length
option c: area; the djeba; a unit of length;
option d: area; the djeba, a unit of length;
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A semicolon after 'area' and 'length' correctly sets off the parenthetical definitions, which themselves contain commas.

question:
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
Jane Austen's well-known 1813 novel, centered on a young woman named Elizabeth Bennet, carries a title many readers recognize at once: Pride and Prejudice. The book, however, was first meant to bear a different ______ during the writing and revising, Austen had intended to name it First Impressions.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A comma sets off the interrupter 'though,' and a semicolon then joins the two independent clauses.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? Although the ensembles Intocable and Banda el Recodo are frequently lumped together under the broad "regional Mexican music" heading, each keeps to its own separate musical lineage. Intocable works within the norteno tradition, which arose in northern Mexico during the late nineteenth century. Banda el Recodo, ______ belongs to the banda tradition, whose roots lie in the southern and central Mexico of the mid-nineteenth century.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The sentence contrasts the second group's tradition with the first, so a contrast transition fits.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? The National Heritage Fellowship was established to recognize outstanding folk and traditional artists in the United States. In 2004 the Irish American accordionist Joe Derrane received the fellowship in order to ______ the contributions he had made to the arts over his lifetime.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: An award honoring an artist's lifetime work serves to celebrate those contributions.

question:
As used in the text, what does the word "constantly" most nearly mean? The following text is adapted from Willa Cather's 1912 novel Alexander's Bridge.
Over the following days Alexander stayed very busy. He took a desk at the office of a [Scottish] engineering firm on Henrietta Street and worked almost constantly. He kept away from the clubs and generally ate dinner by himself at his hotel.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Working 'almost constantly' means working nearly without stopping.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? The consonant inventories of the Pacific's Polynesian languages lean toward the ______: Tongan, spoken in the South Pacific, has twelve consonants in all, and olelo Hawaii, the language of the Native Hawaiian people, has four fewer than that, whereas the worldwide median for a language exceeds twenty-two.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Consonant counts well below the global median indicate an inventory that is minimal.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? In Puerto Rico a number of farmers and other business owners have embraced agritourism as a way of ______ rural economies. Chocolate-loving tourists can now graft cacao varieties at Hacienda Jeanmarie Chocolat or take part in a cacao festival at Hacienda Buena Vista--offerings that generate work beyond conventional farming and channel more tourist spending into the local communities.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Creating jobs and drawing in tourist dollars strengthens, or fortifies, rural economies.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? Biologist Bryson Voirin and colleagues have used hat-shaped monitors to ______ long-held misconceptions about how active sloths really are. People once widely assumed that the pale-throated three-toed sloth and other sloths sleep the whole day. The monitors' data show that, in the wild, sloths actually sleep roughly nine hours a day.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Data contradicting the old belief serve to dispel that misconception.

question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole? In the United States the Lanham Act permits companies to hold trademarks, which are words or images that stand for particular products. "Q-tips," for instance, denotes products manufactured specifically by Unilever, the company holding that trademark. However, the Lanham Act also permits a trademark to be revoked if it stops being specific. "Zipper," for example, was once a trademark for one brand of clothing fastener. Over time, however, people began applying "zipper" to many different brands. Because the word had turned generic, a court ruled that it could no longer be owned as a trademark.
option a: It adds to the text's description of products made by Unilever.
option b: It completes the text's comparison of trademark laws in the US to laws in other countries.
option c: It concludes the text's argument about how the Lanham Act can be improved.
option d: It begins the text's discussion of the fact that trademarks can be taken away.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The sentence introduces the idea, developed by the 'zipper' example, that a trademark can be revoked.

question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole? Celebrated for the albums Quiet Nights and Sketches of Spain, jazz trumpeter Miles Davis worked with pianist Gil Evans on several occasions. Their 1958 reworking of George Gershwin's opera Porgy and Bess bears little resemblance to the 1935 original. Davis and Evans had no wish to satisfy listeners who expected the opera to be reproduced exactly. They dropped sections, such as the aria "I Got Plenty of Nuthin'," and at times only gestured briefly toward Gershwin's melodies. Yet their readiness to recompose Gershwin's material produced one of the most lasting albums in Davis's body of work.
option a: It shows why two musicians benefited from ignoring certain conventions.
option b: It explains how one musician's work influenced another's.
option c: It describes an attitude that influenced the artistic decisions of two musicians.
option d: It establishes a relationship between two musicians.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The sentence captures the musicians' disregard for exact duplication, an attitude shaping the choices described afterward.

question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole? In 2015 Floriana Lai and colleagues published a study concluding that ocean acidification strongly affects the behavior of Gasterosteus aculeatus, a species of fish. However, Lai and colleagues' study drew on an average sample size of only 12 fish. In a 2022 review of various scientists' conclusions about how ocean acidification affects fish behavior, Jeff C. Clements and colleagues warn that leaning on such a comparatively small sample size can raise the chance of biased analysis. That kind of analysis, in turn, can feed into reports of exaggerated effects.
option a: It summarizes a shift in scientists' understanding of how Gasterosteus aculeatus has responded to ocean acidification.
option b: It elaborates on a potential consequence of Lai and colleagues' reliance on a relatively small sample size.
option c: It emphasizes the magnitude of the effect reported by Lai and colleagues of ocean acidification on Gasterosteus aculeatus.
option d: It counters the objection of Clements and colleagues to studies that rely on relatively small sample sizes.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The sentence traces how the small sample can lead to biased analysis and thus exaggerated effects.

question:
Based on the text, which statement is true of the speaker and her friend? The following text is from Anne Spencer's 1922 poem "Translation."
We trekked into a far country, My friend and I. Our deeper content was never spoken, But each knew all the other said. He told me how calm his soul was laid By the lack of anvil and strife. "The wooing kestrel," I said, "mutes his mating-note To please the harmony of this sweet silence."
option a: They understand one another's feelings without having to explicitly discuss them.
option b: They think nature is much less interesting than being in a dynamic city.
option c: They once felt more closely connected to one another than they do now.
option d: They regard the natural world as a place of both peace and conflict.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Our deeper content was never spoken, But each knew all the other said' shows they grasp each other's feelings without stating them.

question: Which statement about bison and elk dung samples is best supported by the text? Moose have a fecal-steroidal profile that is plainly distinct from that of other ungulates, bison and elk included. Bison dung, by contrast, cannot be told apart from elk dung on the basis of fecal-steroidal profiles alone, since both contain comparable amounts of beta-sitosterol and cholestanone, among other sterols. Levels of certain taxa-specific digestive by-products, however, such as cholic acid, can help distinguish bison samples from elk samples.
option a: They are distinct from each other with respect to both cholestanone and cholic acid content, but bison and moose samples cannot be distinguished from each other based solely on levels of digestive by-products.
option b: They are distinct from each other with respect to cholic acid content but cannot otherwise be distinguished from moose samples based solely on levels of digestive by-products.
option c: They are more distinct with respect to beta-sitosterol content than they are with respect to cholic acid content.
option d: They are less distinct with respect to their steroidal profiles than they are with respect to some other digestive by-products.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Bison and elk match on steroidal profile but differ in cholic acid, so they are less distinct in profile than in that by-product.

question:
Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the assertion?
Annual Mean Forest Patch Size for Three Land Use Capability Classes in the Chorotega Region, Costa Rica (graph; x-axis Year: 1960, 1979, 1986, 2000; y-axis Mean patch size (hectares), 0 to 125; series: Class I-IV (suitable for crops), Class VI (severe limitations on use for crops), Class VII (very severe limitations on use for crops)).
To gauge how much deforestation had taken place in Costa Rica's Chorotega region, Juan Pablo Arroyo-Mora and colleagues drew on historical aerial photography and remote sensing data to follow shifts in the annual mean size of forest patches across various land use capability classes (categories signaling the possible uses of forest land). Because of the region's climate, many kinds of forested land were converted to cattle pasture as climbing international meat prices fueled a cattle-ranching boom during the 1960s and 1970s. By 1986 mean forest patch sizes had fallen sharply. That year, they stood between ______
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: By 1986 the graphed mean patch sizes had dropped into the 0-to-50-hectare range.

question:
Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the students' conclusion?
A biology class investigated why individual house mice (Mus musculus) can differ from one another in their blood's mature B cell concentration. The students compared wild-type mice with knockout mice--mice that have particular genes switched off--placing mice of each kind in comparable naturalistic settings and drawing blood periodically. Because knockout mice with the gene Arhgap17 deactivated tended to show lower mature B cell counts than the wild-type mice did, the students concluded that differences in mature B cell concentration among house mice in nature are due solely to variation in how strongly Arhgap17 is expressed.
option a: The mice with Arhgap17 deactivated were identical to the wild-type mice except with regard to mature B cell concentration.
option b: The level of expression of Arhgap17 does not appear to affect the functioning of any other genes in house mice.
option c: Some wild-type mice were very similar to the knockout mice with regard to mature B cell concentration but showed a wide variety of levels of expression of Arhgap17.
option d: A sampling of house mice captured in natural settings shows that individual mice can differ from one another in the level of expression of Arhgap17.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Similar B cell counts paired with widely varying Arhgap17 expression shows the gene is not the sole cause.

question:
Which statement, if true, would most strongly support the claim in the underlined sentence?
Philosopher Ingrid Robeyns defends the principle of limitarianism--the idea that there should be a ceiling on how much wealth any single person can accumulate. Opponents of limitarianism reply that it is unworkable, since it would demand both a universal, strict individual commitment to a code of ethics and worldwide cooperation among governments in areas such as economic policy, neither of which is at all likely. But some defenders of limitarianism hold that, even if these objections have merit, they do not undermine limitarianism's value as a moral goal toward which we may be able to make some progress.
option a: If one agrees that it is undesirable for a very small percentage of a society's population to have a very large percentage of that society's wealth, then it must therefore be desirable to place an upper limit on the wealth a person can have so that a society's wealth is more evenly distributed.
option b: There are reasons why a limited amount of difference in the wealth that people possess should be tolerated if not encouraged--for example, some jobs are more dangerous than others, and those jobs should therefore earn a higher income than others.
option c: Successfully practicing limitarianism involves several categories of actions (structural actions, such as reforming institutions to provide a livable minimum wage; fiscal actions, such as implementing a progressive tax on wealth; and ethical actions, such as choosing to give away one's wealth) and none of these actions will suffice alone.
option d: Most of our societal ideals are regulative ideals, suggesting results that we ought to aim for even if they cannot be fully realized; for example, just because strategies to reduce poverty can never be completely effective for everyone does not mean it is foolish to attempt to reduce poverty.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Treating limitarianism as a regulative ideal worth pursuing despite being unattainable directly backs the claim.

question:
Which choice most logically completes the text?
The great blue heron and the small dark heron are long-legged birds that live in wetlands, such as the Everglades in Florida. Laura D'Acunto and colleagues wanted to learn how these birds select an area in which to live. They examined features of the birds' habitats, such as the area's geographic location and how deep the water is during breeding season. They found that, although both great blue herons and small dark herons prefer areas that hold standing water for more than 60 days per year, only great blue herons prefer areas with deep water during breeding season, suggesting that ______
option a: having features that are highly attractive to one species will likely cause an area to be avoided by the other species.
option b: the effect of water depth on an area's appeal to the two species increases with the duration of the presence of standing water, but more strongly for great blue herons than for small dark herons.
option c: outside of breeding season, both species show a stronger preference for areas with shallower water.
option d: merely having standing water for at least a certain number of days per year will not necessarily make an area equally attractive to both species.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Because water depth appeals only to great blue herons, shared standing water alone does not make an area equally attractive to both.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? According to a 2017 analysis by economist Jacob Lundberg, the top US tax rate of 48% was lower than the peak of the country's Laffer curve (76%). For some economists, whether a tax cut ______ US tax revenue hinges on where the country sits on the Laffer curve, a theoretical relationship between tax rates and revenues.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The subordinate clause needs a finite verb, so 'will ultimately raise or lower' is required.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Under the Electoral College system, all 10 of Missouri's electoral votes go to the US presidential candidate who wins the state's popular ______ in the US Constitution, the Electoral College is a permanent feature of US politics. However, a 2001 article by law professors Akhil and Vikram Amar argues that this system could be changed from within--if states agree to allocate their electoral votes to the winner of the national popular vote.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A period ends the first complete sentence, and 'Inscribed' begins a new one with a modifier.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Whereas French philosopher Michel de Montaigne's essay "Of Quick or Slow Speech" examines a relatively light ______ his essay "Of Liberty of Conscience" takes on weightier material.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A single comma correctly separates the introductory 'Whereas' clause from the main clause.
